data.name: Samant
data.gender_notes: Samant is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Samant is a Sanskrit name derived from the Sanskrit word ‘Samanta’ which means expansive or extensive. It is a powerful name that symbolizes all-encompassing and all-knowing. It is also associated with wisdom and strength. The name Samant carries the meaning “Expansive, Extensive, All-Encompassing” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Marathi, Hindi. Parents who choose Samant usually hope their child will grow to embody expansive, extensive, all-encompassing and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Samant is a sacred name in Hinduism, signifying the infinite and the all-knowing. It is believed to bring wisdom, power, and strength to the bearer.
data.etymology: Samant belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Expansive, Extensive, All-Encompassing.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Samant total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: In Hindu tradition, the name Samant holds a significant cultural impact as it reflects the idea of universal consciousness and vast knowledge. It is often given to children as a reminder of their vast potential and limitless possibilities. Furthermore, the name is also associated with royalty and nobility, as samant means "most excellent" or "great man" in Prakrit language. Thus, bearing the name Samant is a source of pride and accomplishment, instilling a sense of grandeur and significance in the bearer.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Samant symbolizes the infinite and eternal nature of the soul. It is a reminder of the expansiveness and depth of the divine consciousness that resides within each individual. The name also reflects the power of the mind to comprehend the vastness of the universe and the wisdom to navigate through life's complexities. Ultimately, the name Samant serves as a call to expand one's awareness and understanding of the self and the world around us, leading to a deeper connection with the divine.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Samant in Sanskrit translates to 'all-pervading' or 'encompassing'. It symbolizes the concept of being boundless and all-inclusive, representing the divine presence in all aspects of life.

historical_references.reference: King Samant Sahai of the Chandela Dynasty ruled over the Malwa region in central India between 1063 and 1068 CE. He is known for his military conquests and the construction of several temples, including the famous Mahakaleshwar Temple in Ujjain.
historical_references.context: Chandela Dynasty, Malwa region, Military conquests, Temple construction

historical_references.reference: Samantarma Chola, also known as Rajaraja Kulothunga Chola I, was a powerful ruler of the Chola Empire in the late 12th century CE. He is celebrated for his military victories, architecture, and literary patronage. Samantarma is believed to have assumed the throne around 1178 CE and ruled until 1216 CE.
historical_references.context: Chola Empire, Military victories, Architecture, Literary patronage

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Samant' is an ancient Hindu title which translates to 'great' or 'gracious'. In modern contexts, this title is often used on social media platforms by individuals to convey a sense of nobility or high status. In the business world, 'Samant' is the surname of several notable business families in India, suggesting a long lineage of wealth and power. In politics, 'Samant' is used to refer to powerful leaders, particularly in the Indian state of Odisha, where the title is still in use as a hereditary title for certain communities.
